Install and lint both Markdown surfaces
value.run:
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

# Do not load user/system Git credentials or hooks during anonymous acquisition.
$env:GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM = '1'
$env:GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL = '/dev/null'
$env:GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT = '0'
if (-not [string]::IsNullOrEmpty($env:GITHUB_TOKEN) -or
    -not [string]::IsNullOrEmpty($env:GH_TOKEN) -or
    -not [string]::IsNullOrEmpty($env:ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN)) {
    throw 'credential-policy: a token was projected into a code job'
}
if (Test-Path Variable:PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference) {
    $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $false
}

# Fixed paths into the distribution the previous step downloaded and
# verified against a reviewed digest, rather than a PATH lookup.
# Get-Command consults the command table and PATH, and this is the
# step that runs repository-controlled code, so resolving through
# either would let that code choose which node runs. The bin
# directory is still prepended to PATH because npm's shim resolves
# its interpreter through env.
$strNodeRoot = [System.IO.Path]::Combine($env:RUNNER_TEMP, 'node24')
$strNodePath = [System.IO.Path]::Combine($strNodeRoot, 'bin', 'node')
$strNpmPath = [System.IO.Path]::Combine($strNodeRoot, 'bin', 'npm')
if (-not [System.IO.File]::Exists($strNodePath) -or -not [System.IO.File]::Exists($strNpmPath)) {
    throw 'toolchain: the reviewed Node distribution is not present'
}
$env:PATH = [System.IO.Path]::Combine($strNodeRoot, 'bin') + [System.IO.Path]::PathSeparator + $env:PATH
$strNodeVersion = (& $strNodePath --version).Trim()
$intNodeVersionExit = $LASTEXITCODE
$strNpmVersion = (& $strNpmPath --version).Trim()
$intNpmVersionExit = $LASTEXITCODE
if ($intNodeVersionExit -ne 0 -or $strNodeVersion -cne 'v24.18.1') {
    throw "toolchain: node version check failed with exit $intNodeVersionExit"
}
if ($intNpmVersionExit -ne 0 -or $strNpmVersion -cne '11.16.0') {
    throw "toolchain: npm version check failed with exit $intNpmVersionExit"
}
Write-Host "Node executable: $strNodePath ($strNodeVersion)"
Write-Host "npm executable: $strNpmPath ($strNpmVersion)"

# Reviewed baseline. The before/after comparison further below proves
# only that npm ci left these files alone; it cannot detect metadata
# that was already altered at review time. This gate runs before
# installation so unreviewed scripts are never installed and never run.
$strReviewedPackageHash = '59E676D981CFFA350CB72E7EA4B1AEEC2C49D56621958A095AA0E76733EC2CD9'
$strReviewedLockHash = '5EFC1286025CDC3AD03796C5F4E44CC697E674A30E61DE05E299B2A30ABAD1A2'
$strPackageBefore = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath package.json -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
$strLockBefore = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath package-lock.json -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
if ($strPackageBefore -cne $strReviewedPackageHash -or $strLockBefore -cne $strReviewedLockHash) {
    throw 'supply: package metadata does not match the reviewed supply digest'
}

# npm reads .npmrc from the project directory before it runs anything,
# and script-shell there replaces the interpreter for every npm run. A
# pull request can add one without altering either reviewed digest or
# any governed workflow, after which both lint phases exit zero with the
# command echoed and no linter ever executed. No .npmrc is reviewed in
# this repository, so any is refused here, ahead of installation, so npm
# never reads one.
foreach ($strNpmConfigPath in @('.npmrc', '../.npmrc', '../../.npmrc')) {
    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $strNpmConfigPath) {
        throw 'supply: repository-controlled npm configuration is present'
    }
}

# The loop above walks project paths, which is where a committed
# .npmrc would sit -- but npm also loads a per-user file at
# $HOME/.npmrc and a global one, and neither is under the repository
# tree. A script-shell setting in either replaces the interpreter for
# every npm run, so both lint phases would exit zero with the command
# echoed and no linter executed, leaving installation, asset hashes,
# the policy validator and all three captured statuses intact.
# Enumerating those paths would be another list to be one entry
# short of, so npm is told where to read them from instead. Both are
# pointed at /dev/null rather than at an absent name: an absent name
# under RUNNER_TEMP is absent only until something creates it, and the
# first lint phase is repository-adjacent code that runs before the
# second one reads the file. /dev/null always reads as empty and no
# unprivileged process can make it read as anything else, so the
# neutralization holds across both phases instead of only until the
# check that observed it.
# npm refuses to load one file at two config levels -- it exits
# before config resolution with "double-loading config" -- so the two
# settings cannot both name /dev/null. They use the same property by
# two routes: a source this job cannot write.
$env:npm_config_userconfig = '/dev/null'
$env:npm_config_globalconfig = '/etc/npmrc-absent-by-policy'
if (-not [string]::IsNullOrEmpty((Get-Content -Raw -LiteralPath $env:npm_config_userconfig -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue))) {
    throw 'supply: the neutralized npm configuration source is not empty'
}
if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $env:npm_config_globalconfig) {
    throw 'supply: the neutralized npm configuration path exists'
}
# /dev/null reads as empty. The absent global path is under root-owned
# /etc on the hosted runner. The two distinct sources avoid npm rejecting
# the same file at two configuration levels. Neither lint phase can write
# the global source without a privilege change outside this job contract.
$strGlobalConfigDirectory = [System.IO.Path]::GetDirectoryName($env:npm_config_globalconfig)
if ($strGlobalConfigDirectory -cne '/etc') {
    throw 'supply: the neutralized global npm configuration is not under a root-owned directory'
}

# The reviewed digests above cover what is installed, not what the
# lint actually does. Both lint phases execute from the checkout: the
# rule configuration decides which rules run at all, and the
# nested-fence helper is the whole of the second phase. A pull
# request editing either keeps every npm command string, every
# captured status, and every digest intact while both phases report
# zero errors over nothing.
$strReviewedLintConfigHash = '5EB07BF7F30829E0091E82F235A96FDBA21BE1EF1160CA1E22CDBE8D82DA5300'
$strReviewedLintHelperHash = 'B20AAAB172224DA4377CDA75FA6CAD1A8EEB00F8BDD26737FFE0E6C2AD222492'
$strLintConfigHash = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath .markdownlint.jsonc -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
$strLintHelperHash = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath lint-nested-markdown.js -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
if ($strLintConfigHash -cne $strReviewedLintConfigHash -or $strLintHelperHash -cne $strReviewedLintHelperHash) {
    throw 'supply: lint configuration or helper does not match the reviewed digest'
}

$boolCiExisted = Test-Path Env:CI
$strPriorCi = $env:CI
try {
    $env:CI = 'true'
    & $strNpmPath ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
    $intInstallExit = $LASTEXITCODE
} finally {
    if ($boolCiExisted) {
        $env:CI = $strPriorCi
    } else {
        Remove-Item Env:CI -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    }
}
if ($intInstallExit -ne 0) { throw "npm-ci: native exit $intInstallExit" }

$strPackageAfterInstall = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath package.json -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
$strLockAfterInstall = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath package-lock.json -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
if ($strPackageAfterInstall -cne $strPackageBefore -or $strLockAfterInstall -cne $strLockBefore) {
    throw 'npm-ci: package metadata changed during frozen installation'
}

# Re-taken after installation and before the phases that read them.
# This asserts one specific thing and no more: that npm ci did not
# disturb the two lint assets between the gate above and the linters
# below. It is not a boundary against a concurrent writer --
# Get-FileHash reads and closes, so any process still running could
# write the file after the hash and before the linter opens it. The
# boundary is established by ordering instead: npm ci installs the
# lockfile-pinned tree with --ignore-scripts, so no repository or
# package code runs between the gate and the linters. The name says
# installation because installation is what it spans. Policy code runs
# only in the separate policy job.
$strLintConfigAfterInstall = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath .markdownlint.jsonc -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
$strLintHelperAfterInstall = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath lint-nested-markdown.js -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
if ($strLintConfigAfterInstall -cne $strReviewedLintConfigHash -or $strLintHelperAfterInstall -cne $strReviewedLintHelperHash) {
    throw 'supply: lint configuration or helper changed during installation'
}

& $strNpmPath run lint:md
$intOuterExit = $LASTEXITCODE
Write-Host "outer-markdown native exit: $intOuterExit"

& $strNpmPath run lint:md:nested
$intNestedExit = $LASTEXITCODE
Write-Host "nested-markdown native exit: $intNestedExit"

$strPackageFinal = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath package.json -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
$strLockFinal = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath package-lock.json -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
if ($strPackageFinal -cne $strPackageBefore -or $strLockFinal -cne $strLockBefore) {
    throw 'validation: package metadata changed after installation or linting'
}
if ($intOuterExit -ne 0 -or $intNestedExit -ne 0) {
    throw 'validation: one or more lint phases failed'
}
